intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that osteogenesis imperfecta type X (OI10) is caused by homozygous mutation in the SERPINH1 gene, which encodes the collagen chaperone protein HSP47.

paragraphs.text: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X (OI10) is an autosomal recessive form of OI caused by mutation in SERPINH1, which encodes the type I procollagen chaperone HSP47 (Christiansen et al., 2010). Duran et al. (2015) stated that mutations in SERPINH1 mostly cause a moderately severe form of OI. The severe phenotype reported by Christiansen et al. (2010) was described as severe recessive OI.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with severe OI, Christiansen et al. (2010) identified a homozygous missense mutation in the SERPINH1 gene (c.233T-C; leu78-to-pro, L78P). The mutation caused degradation of HSP47, an endoplasmic reticulum resident protein, through the proteasome. In fibroblasts from the affected individual, type I procollagen built up in the Golgi, and part of the secreted type I procollagen was protease sensitive. Prolyl residue 986 in the triple helical domain of proalpha1(I) chains showed normal 3-hydroxylation. The authors concluded that HSP47 functions downstream of the CRTAP/P3H1/CyPB complex that carries out prolyl 3-hydroxylation.

paragraphs.text: Duran et al. (2015) identified a new OI mutation in SERPINH1 that destabilized and mislocalized HSP47. The mutation had similar secondary effects on FKBP65, the type I procollagen chaperone encoded by FKBP10. In cells with mutant HSP47, HSP47 and FKBP65 did not interact properly.

paragraphs.text: Christiansen et al. (2010) proposed that HSP47 checks the integrity of the type I procollagen triple helix at the ER/cis-Golgi boundary. In their model, when HSP47 is absent, procollagen moves from the ER to the Golgi faster than normal and its helical structure is compromised.

paragraphs.text: Duran et al. (2015) found evidence that HSP47 and FKBP65 work together during posttranslational maturation of type I procollagen. They concluded that OI caused by HSP47 deficiency and OI caused by FKBP65 deficiency share a common cellular pathway.

checks.evidence_quote: These results thus reveal a common cellular pathway in cases of OI caused by HSP47 and FKBP65 deficiency.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with severe autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta type X (OI10), Christiansen et al. (2010) identified a homozygous c.233T-C transition in the SERPINH1 gene, resulting in a leu78-to-pro (L78P) substitution. The mutant HSP47 protein was degraded by the proteasome. In the patient's fibroblasts, type I procollagen accumulated in the Golgi, and a fraction of the secreted type I procollagen was protease sensitive.
